short_outcome: Yale AI Club asked for 20 CC-HOOD-NAVY, size M, with a bulk discount. Inventory found only 8 on hand -- a 12-unit shortfall no tool can fabricate away -- and computed that a 25%-off price ($43.50) clears the shop's 1.3x-unit-cost floor ($28.60), so the discount itself is policy-compliant. But the quantity gap is a real-world business decision (accept 8 now? wait for restock? decline?) outside any agent's authority or any tool this system has, so Boss confirmed the numbers and left the ticket at needs_approval, asking the requester to revise the quantity to 8 or fewer or propose a specific, policy-compliant price.

agent_contributions.boss: Delegated the ticket to Inventory. When Inventory escalated the quantity shortfall, independently re-verified the stock count and pricing, confirmed Inventory's math, and closed the ticket with a clear ask back to the requester rather than inventing a resolution.
agent_contributions.inventory: Verified on-hand stock (8, vs. 20 requested) and pricing (unit cost $22.00, list $58.00), computed the maximum allowed discount (25% off, floor of 1.3x cost), and escalated to Boss rather than silently shrinking the order or approving a bigger discount than policy allows.

human_approval.reason: This isn't a cash payment -- it's a quantity/pricing judgment call the dashboard's Approve flow has no mechanism for. No proposal of any kind was created.

note: Left honestly at needs_approval rather than forced to a fake 'resolved' -- the team correctly identified it lacks the authority (and the shop lacks the inventory) to fully close this ticket on its own. See the Problem 10 reflection for what tooling would actually unblock it.
